newsitem.title: USA: CFTC okays listing 4 more S&P 500 contract months.
newsitem.headline: CFTC okays listing 4 more S&P 500 contract months.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has approved listing four more contract months for Standard and Poor's 500 stock index futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, the CME reported Wednesday.

The CME said the additional contracts would allow trading in long-dated flexible options. CME rules dictate that the underlying futures contract for a flexible option shall be any S&P 500 futures contract that is currently available for trading. Thus, when the four additional contracts are listed, flexible options based on those contracts will be eligible for trading, the CME said.
The CME will list the four additional contracts -- June, September and December 1998 and March 1999 -- beginning May 27.
The CFTC also approved adding four strikes up and down -- eight strikes in all -- for all options on the S&P 500 futures index trading on GLOBEX, beginning Sunday night, June 1, the CME said.

Currently, one contract month in the March expiration cycle and two months not in that cycle are listed on GLOBEX for S&P 500 options. Six strikes up and down from the at-the-money strike are available for each month during GLOBEX, while 12 strikes are available up and down during regular trading hours.

"Because of recent high volatilities in the S&P contracts, market participants have stated that adding four more strikes up and down for each contract would provide more trading opportunities," the CME said in an executive report Wednesday.
